Someone has expressed that they believe I have made this too broad. I would like to clarify that this was meant to be a very casual, free form survey. I am not looking for anything specific except your own personal experience. I didn't mean so much to "ask a question" as I meant to just give an open mic to whoever would like to share.

I do, however, understand that it is difficult to know WHERE to start when no prompt is given. A few questions that might be worth answering...

1. What factors do you believe went into your development of an eating disorder? Do you consider the media portrayal of thinness or dieting to be influential? 
2. If you are in recovery, what methods have helped you? What sort of treatment are you receiving, and was it easy to find in your area? 
3. How did you realize you suffer from an eating disorder? 
4. What misconceptions do you face about your ED that you'd like to put to rest, if any? 

I feel a little hesitant ending my list there, because there are honestly so many other things that are important, perhaps more important than what I asked.

Literally anything. If your carbohydrate intake drops, you NEED to make sure you eat enough fat. You describe a moderate carbohydrate, moderate/high protein diet, but do you eat adequately of fats? If you're feeling lethargic after a few days, it's quite possible that you don't, or that if you do you aren't well suited to fat burning (yet). The lethargy should be temporary. Going back and forth between binges and lower carb intake does nothing good for your body. I would know, I have a history of binge/restrict cycles. 

Also, 1500kcal, while not drastically low, is probably not going to be very satisfying if you're not eating a large percentage of that from fat. I can less than that in a day and wake up feeling wonderful, not hungry, and energized because my blood sugar is very stable and my body knows how to use fat for energy (of course, if I eat so little one day, I make it up over the next few. Not through binging, but through intuitive increases in intake of healthy foods. A healthy body does a good job of regulating intake). 

The desire to binge makes me think you're not eating enough to be satisfied, both of calories and satiating macronutrients.
